The turf thing is easy to explain ...

• Cost of stadiums EXPLODED. NRG opened in 2002 at a cost of $352 million ... Lucas Oil opened in 2008 for $732M ... MetLife in 2010 at $1.6B ... and so on.

• To justify stadium costs, owners increasingly jammed more events in them.

• Grass is difficult to maintain if you're putting a million events in the stadiums.

• Turf is easier and cheaper.

• More teams do it, it becomes normalized, so then others, like the Panthers and Titans, take advantage of that to save money.

And here we are. Reality is, even if you set the safety issue aside, players hate the way they feel coming off playing on it. There's a reason why 32 out of 32 teams practice on grass, even when they're preparing to play for a game on turf.

It'll be interesting to see where this goes from here.
